mike: Heads-up — CI microbench on PR #18111 shows a cross-env warmup variance. shadow1 +12% batch_latency, shadow2 -22% kv_cache_hit_rate. This started after the kernel-autoselect tweak in the PR. :eyes:
ci-bot: Job <https://ci.internal.redwood/pr/18111/build/412|pr-18111/microbench> failed 3/5 thresholds. Diff summary attached.
perf-bot: Threshold diffs:
```
> batch_latency.p50: +12.3% (thresh +5%)
> kv_cache_hit_rate: -22.1% (thresh -5%)
> kernel_switch_count: +45
```
anna: Repro locally on a small shadow run? I can try `./scripts/run_microbench --env=shadow2 --suite=warmup --reps=10` and attach flamegraph.
leo: I noticed kernel-autoselect path picks `quant-v2` on shadow1 but `fp16-legacy` on shadow2 for same model/seq_len distribution. Autoselect heuristics changed in the PR to prefer smaller kernels for short seqs — maybe that's flipping warmup/warm-cache behavior.
tara: We should bisect the PR changes around the kernel selection heuristics vs scheduler warmup tweak. I can run a quick regtest series.
mike: plan: 1) reproduce in shadow2 locally (anna), 2) bisect commit range in PR branch (tara), 3) try gate that disables auto-quant for seq_len < 64 (leo/sofia), 4) hold rollout if confirmed.
sofia: shadow2 reproduces — kv hit drops ~22% within 30s of steady traffic. Snapshot of metrics: `kv.hits=7800, kv.misses=2800` => hit_rate 73% vs baseline 95%.
ops-bot: pausing canary rollout for pr-18111 per request from @mike — flag: `canary.pause=true` set. :no_entry_sign:
mike: can someone run `git bisect` across the PR? suspected commits: kernel_autoselect.c heuristic rewrite + scheduler warmup reorder. Example bisect step: `git bisect start -- pr/18111 HEAD -- good main~5`
anna: quick flamegraph (uploaded): <https://profiler.internal/redwood/fg/18111/shot1>. Top hotspot shows `allocator::fast_alloc` thrashing around batch coalescer path.
leo: allocator thrash + kernel flip explains cache churn. If kernel changes increase per-request allocation pattern, KV cache lines get invalidated/evicted earlier. Suggest skip-autoselect for quant kernels when `seq_len <= 64` as a trial.
sofia: made a local patch to short-circuit autoselect: `if (seq_len <= 64 && kernel_family==quant) use baseline_kernel;` Quick run shows kv_hit back to 91% and batch_latency down ~7%.
tara: I'll push a quick WIP PR with the guard and run the full microbench CI — tagging `priority/rollout-blocker`.
mike: good. If CI confirms, we'll ship hotfix and continue bisect for a proper fix. If CI still noisy, we revert the original autoselect commit.
perf-bot: CI (wip-guard) results available: <https://ci.internal.redwood/pr/18112/build/3|pr-18112/microbench> — batch_latency.p50: -6.9% vs failing run, kv_cache_hit_rate: +17.8% (within thresholds).
ops-bot: canary.resume cleared after positive wip run, but marking manual hold until nightly canary passes.
mike: thanks everyone. Keep the bisect artifacts in the PR and add the metric snapshots. We'll leave this thread open until the canary has been green for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
